title: E0056: Weak randomness for security-sensitive value
plain_english: Functions such as `rand()`, `mt_rand()`, and `uniqid()` are predictable. They are not suitable for tokens, passwords, salts, nonces, or other secrets, even though they may be fine for games or non-security sampling.
why_matters: Predictable values can be guessed or brute-forced, which may expose password-reset links, CSRF tokens, session identifiers, API keys, or other sensitive data.
what_it_checks: Assignments to variables whose names look security-sensitive, such as `token`, `secret`, `password`, `nonce`, `salt`, `csrf`, or `api_key`
Values passed to `password_hash()`, `hash_hmac()`, `hash()`, `openssl_encrypt()`, `openssl_sign()`, cookie functions, or session ID functions
